<details>
<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

Four boxes, each drawn inside the next. **Level 1 Standard** is the innermost. **Level 2 Enhanced**
contains it. **Level 3 Comprehensive** contains both. **Level 4 BCA** contains all three. The
nesting is the point: the checks in a box are *additional to* everything inside it, not instead of
it. Twenty-nine checks in all.

**Level 1 Standard**, the innermost box. Seven checks start here. Produce the analysis well and
record enough that someone could re-run it. *Reviewed by* a colleague, within your team. *Sign-off:*
no formal sign-off beyond you, and a quality assurance statement is optional. *The seven checks:*
validation of requirements; specification, user guide and notes; data sources and assumptions clear;
accuracy of data transformations and calculations; methodological correctness; sense checking
results; clarity, accessibility and security of outputs.

**Level 2 Enhanced** contains Level 1 and adds nine checks. What the step up buys is separation from
the work. *Reviewed by* someone who had no hand in producing the work. *Sign-off:* your team lead,
with the reviewer named before the work starts and a quality assurance statement required. *The nine
checks:* responsibilities and accountabilities; appropriateness of methodology; documentation and
audit trails; understanding of the impacts of data quality; evidence based assumptions; code
scrutiny; validation with stakeholders and subject matter experts; sensitivity testing;
triangulation and independent validation of results.

**Level 3 Comprehensive** contains Levels 1 and 2 and adds eight checks. What the step up buys is
separation from the team, and published transparency. *Reviewed by* an assurer from outside the
delivering team. *Sign-off:* the Head of Profession or Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, with the statement
published with the output and a review date set. *The eight checks:* change control processes;
ethical risks; knowledge sharing; detailed documentation review; usability testing; automated
checks; additional scenario testing; independent peer review.

**Level 4 BCA**, the outermost box, contains all of the above and adds five checks. Business
Critical work only. *Reviewed by* a Lead Assurer from outside the delivering team, with external
review. *Sign-off:* the Lead Assurer, then the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, with a register
entry required. *The five checks:* formal audits; external review; additional scrutiny of
documentation; scrutiny of structural and conceptual assumptions; additional scenario testing, which
is listed at Level 3 and again here.

**A Level is not a tier.** A tier is one band of activity. A Level includes every level below it as
well as its own. Reading Tier 3 as Level 3 would mean doing the third band and none of the two
beneath it, which is why this playbook uses *Level* throughout.
[Section 5](/guidance/05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) sets the level; this is what it buys you.

**Why the Level 4 BCA block is short.** Everything that is true only of Business Critical work,
including the register entry, the quality assurance appraisal and the documentation stack, is in
[section 8](/guidance/08-business-critical/index.qmd) rather than repeated here. If you scored 4 on any
impact dimension, do the Level 3 block and then go there.

The checks are NHSBSA's own, from the assurance level decision sheet. What each one means in
practice is in the table below. Your quality assurance log records which you did, when, and what you
found.

</details>
